prTitle: Enhanced Pagination Performance for High-Volume Audit Logs
head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17

tps.bug: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
tps.evidenciaOpus: When enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices queryset[cursor.offset:stop] directly (paginator.py:877-882) under a comment claiming the ORM 'properly handles negative slicing'; Django querysets reject negative indices, so such cursors raise instead of paginating.
tps.evidenciaAstra: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877-882 forwards negative offsets directly into Django queryset slicing, which rejects negative indices. Cursor parsing permits these offsets at src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:59, and src/sentry/api/base.py:540 catches only BadPaginationError, leaving this failure unhandled.

tps.bug: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
tps.evidenciaOpus: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to getattr(item, self.key) (paginator.py:838-840), and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value, but the only caller uses order_by='-datetime' (organization_auditlogs.py:76-82); math.floor on a datetime raises TypeError while building the cursor for any non-empty page.
tps.evidenciaAstra: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:79-80 selects the new paginator with datetime ordering, but src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838-843 applies numeric rounding directly and returns unconverted cursor values. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a DateTimeField at src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69, so nonempty first pages fail during cursor construction.

tps.bug: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
tps.evidenciaOpus: organization_auditlogs.py:71 evaluates organization_context.member.has_global_access unconditionally for non-superusers, but RpcUserOrganizationContext.member can be None for org auth token / API key requests, so the endpoint raises AttributeError even when optimized_pagination is not requested.
tps.evidenciaAstra: src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/impl.py:123-140 leaves member=None without a user ID, while src/sentry/auth/access.py:1183-1194 supports organization-token access. The unconditional dereference at src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 therefore crashes authorized non-superuser requests without membership, even when optimized pagination is absent.

tps.bug: A user-controlled optimized_pagination flag lets any member with global access switch to a paginator that accepts unvalidated negative cursor offsets, widening the attack surface and causing server errors.
tps.evidenciaOpus: A request-controlled optimized_pagination=true flag (organization_auditlogs.py:70-83) switches any member with global access, not only admins, to the paginator that forwards user-supplied negative cursor offsets into queryset slicing (paginator.py:877-882) with no validation, letting callers trigger server errors; the 'permissions are checked at the queryset level' claim has no backing check.
tps.evidenciaAstra: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70-82 enables the unchecked negative-slicing branch at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877-882 for eligible callers, causing server errors on crafted offsets. OrganizationAuditPermission still enforces access at src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:110-124, so the supported defect is invalid-offset handling rather than an authorization bypass.

tps.bug: BasePaginator.get_result clamps negative offsets only for next cursors; a prev cursor with a negative offset is passed straight into the queryset slice, which Django rejects with an error (500) on every paginated endpoint.
tps.evidenciaOpus: paginator.py:182 clamps the offset only when not cursor.is_prev and passes a negative offset unchanged into queryset[start_offset:stop] for prev cursors; Cursor accepts any int offset (cursors.py:28). Django rejects negative slicing, so a crafted prev cursor returns a 500, and the PR's added comment (lines 179-181) wrongly claims this is safe.
tps.evidenciaAstra: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-184 leaves negative offsets unchanged for previous cursors and passes them into Django queryset slicing, which rejects them. Cursor parsing accepts negative integers at src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:58-59, and src/sentry/api/base.py:540 catches only BadPaginationError around pagination. Although this failure existed previously, the PR directly changes the implicated slicing code; the claim about every paginated endpoint is overly broad.

tps.bug: OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value, which is then compared against the datetime column, so next/prev cursor pagination of audit logs breaks.
tps.evidenciaOpus: paginator.py:842-843: OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns cursor.value, the integer millisecond timestamp, and BasePaginator.build_queryset uses it in the '-datetime' filter. DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor at :238-241 converts it back to a UTC datetime. As a result, following a cursor on the audit-log endpoint filters on the wrong value or fails.
tps.evidenciaAstra: The PR selects OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime" in src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:79-80. Its value_from_cursor returns the numeric value unchanged (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:842-843), which build_queryset inserts directly into the SQL comparison at lines 119-125 against AuditLogEntry's DateTimeField (src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69). Thus timestamp cursors produce an invalid datetime-versus-integer comparison; the required conversion exists in DateTimePaginator at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:238-241.
